glossary.definition: What everything else relies on: here, each chip's meter and secret key.
Hardware quirks unique to each chip that make its key impossible to copy. Simulated here.
The private key signs and never leaves the chip. The public key checks signatures.
The seal. Proves who made a report and that it hasn't changed. Not when, or whether it's complete.
The manufacturer's list of genuine chips, their keys and owners. Listed means endorsed.
One unit of computation. AI jobs run trillions (10¹²).
Kilojoule: the energy the meter records.
Blocking an honest lab (a complaint), or allowing a violation (it slips through).
Goes up by one with every report a chip makes.
A fresh challenge a chip must sign. Pre-signed reports can't use one, so this game uses a counter.
Work done per unit of energy. Training and inference fall in different ranges.

rules.text: Check trust before numbers. Untrusted reports are blocked and never counted.
Charge the chip's registered owner, not the job or record ID.
Limit: {flop_limit} training FLOPs per lab per period.
Inference doesn't count toward the FLOP cap: limits target training, where models gain their capabilities. Energy always counts.
Blocked jobs still count toward totals: the work already ran.
Each level is a new period: totals reset, counters don't.
Accept a report only if its counter beats the last one you accepted from that chip.
Limit: {energy_limit} kJ per lab per period.
The workload type is written by the lab, so check it against the measurements.
Each type has a FLOPs-per-kJ band, with 10% tolerance. Outside it, the claim doesn't fit.
Energy readings are ±5% noisy. Above {energy_margin_limit} kJ counts as over.
